picks.editorial_note: NSF's $90M investment in three new Science and Technology Centers spanning AI, biotech, fusion, and robotics is the week's biggest policy-level commitment to fundamental AI-adjacent research infrastructure, setting the agenda for years of downstream work at dozens of institutions.
picks.title: NSF launches three new Science and Technology Centers with $90M investment in transformative research

picks.editorial_note: SK hynix's $4 billion advanced packaging plant at Purdue is the largest single capital commitment of the week and establishes the first U.S. hub for high-bandwidth memory production, a critical bottleneck input for AI hardware.
picks.title: SK hynix breaks ground on $4 billion advanced packaging production facility in Purdue Research Park

picks.editorial_note: UW's leadership role in three DOE Genesis Mission awards ties university research directly into a 300+ institution national AI-for-science push, signaling how federal AI strategy is being operationalized through academia.
picks.title: UW researchers lead and support 3 new ‘AI-for-Science’ Genesis Mission awards | UW News

picks.editorial_note: The first live use of AI to assist a neurosurgeon in real time during brain tumor surgery is a genuine clinical breakthrough with immediate patient-safety implications, not just a lab demonstration.
picks.title: First patient in live AI-assisted sight-saving brain surgery

picks.editorial_note: UT Austin's new NSF center dedicated to how humans and robots co-adapt tackles a foundational problem for deploying assistive robotics safely and effectively in everyday settings.
picks.title: UT To Lead NSF Center That Will Study How Robots and People Learn To Live and Work Together - UT News
picks.university: The University of Texas at Austin

picks.editorial_note: The Stanford/Arc Institute demonstration that AI can design entirely novel viral genomes raises urgent biosecurity and policy questions that will likely shape AI governance debates well beyond academia.
picks.title: AI Can Now Create Viruses. Should We Let It? - Georgetown University

picks.editorial_note: Suchi Saria's recognition on TIME's 100 most influential people in AI underscores the real-world stakes of her FDA-cleared sepsis early warning system, which has demonstrably reduced patient mortality.
picks.title: Hopkins engineer Suchi Saria among TIME's 100 most influential people in AI

picks.editorial_note: Using AI to hunt for singularities in the Navier-Stokes equations puts machine learning in direct contact with one of mathematics' seven Millennium Prize problems, a striking example of AI advancing pure theory.
picks.title: From the Lab: How Javier Gómez-Serrano is using AI to solve the most elusive question in math

picks.editorial_note: Inria's role in the 31-partner, 14-country euROBIN consortium reflects the scale of Europe's coordinated push to build a shared AI robotics ecosystem across industry, academia, and government.
picks.title: In Brussels, Inria puts European robotics & AI into action with the euROBIN project!

picks.editorial_note: Rochester's role in the $30M NSF TEMPEST center tackles turbulence prediction and control, a longstanding hard physics problem where AI-augmented simulation could have wide engineering payoffs.
picks.title: Can scientists predict—and control—turbulence?
